universal_lens: The system unifies spatial kinematics and computational efficiency via a dual-layer operator: a geometric projection mapping skeletal vectors to biomechanical deviation manifolds, coupled with a knowledge distillation kernel that minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence between high-dimensional teacher potentials and quantized student edge-inference states.

Conformal inference bounds the prediction sets for skeletal keypoints, ensuring that biomechanical error deviations fall within calibrated confidence intervals, thereby providing statistically rigorous, low-latency feedback for automated athletic coaching systems.

primitives.name: Biomechanical Vector Projection Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: The error correction logic relies on rigorous biomechanical modeling, calculating joint angles via vector dot products to identify deviations from professional standards in real-time.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \theta_j: Joint angle (radians), \mathbf{v}_a, \mathbf{v}_b: Skeletal limb vectors (dimensionless pixel coordinates or meters), \cdot: Dot product operator.
primitives.assumptions: Skeletal joints form rigid planar segments; camera calibration allows accurate Euclidean distance approximation in 2D image space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when \|\mathbf{v}_{a}\| or \|\mathbf{v}_{b}\| approaches zero (occluded keypoints) or when vectors are collinear causing loss of angular resolution.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE kinematic constraint solvers, translating raw pixel-space vectors into constrained phase-space trajectories.
layer2.telemetry: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of calculated joint angles against gold-standard motion capture.

primitives.name: Knowledge Distillation Divergence Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: To achieve a balance between high precision and computational efficiency on edge devices, a knowledge distillation framework is employed, where a lightweight MobileNet-V3 student model is trained under the supervision of a high-performance HRNet teacher model.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{L}_{KD}: Distillation loss (dimensionless), T: Temperature scaling parameter (dimensionless), \mathbf{z}_t, \mathbf{z}_s: Teacher/student logits (dimensionless), D_{KL}: KL divergence.
primitives.assumptions: Teacher network provides an optimal, stationary probability distribution over pose configurations; soft labels contain richer structural information than hard labels.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the student architecture lacks the representational capacity to approximate the teacher's decision boundary, leading to catastrophic forgetting or high bias.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI Bayesian model compression, transferring complex prior beliefs from heavy server-side models to lightweight edge priors.
layer2.telemetry: mAP retention rate of the student model compared to the teacher baseline.

primitives.name: Edge Quantization Flow Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: The student model is further optimized using 8-bit integer quantization and the TensorRT inference engine.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: x: Floating point activation (dimensionless), q(x): 8-bit integer activation (uint8), \Delta: Quantization scale factor (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Activation distributions are sufficiently smooth such that uniform quantization introduces bounded, negligible noise to the final pose output.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Precision collapse occurs in the tails of highly skewed activation distributions, causing significant degradation in keypoint localization accuracy.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE low-latency state-update constraints, enforcing strict temporal bounds on the inference loop to guarantee real-time feedback.
layer2.telemetry: Inference latency (ms/frame) and FPS throughput on target mobile hardware.

The mathematical foundation of this real-time coaching system rests on the interplay between geometric rigidity and probabilistic compression. First, the biomechanical state of an athlete is abstracted as a graph of interconnected nodes, where edges represent rigid limbs. The core primitive, `biomech_vector_projection`, utilizes the dot product to compute instantaneous joint angles. This transforms raw 2D pixel coordinates into a constrained angular manifold, allowing the system to quantify deviation from an ideal kinematic template. However, computing these projections requires precise keypoint localization, which is computationally expensive. To resolve this, the `distillation_divergence_kernel` is introduced. It frames the pose estimation task as a density matching problem, minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence between a heavy, high-fidelity teacher network (HRNet) and a lightweight student (MobileNet-V3). This ensures the student inherits the teacher's complex spatial reasoning capabilities. Finally, to satisfy the strict temporal constraints of real-time feedback, the `edge_quantization_flow` operator discretizes the continuous floating-point activations of the student network into 8-bit integers. This introduces a controlled, bounded noise floor but drastically accelerates matrix multiplications via TensorRT. The dualities lie in the trade-off between geometric precision (requiring high-resolution floats) and temporal responsiveness (requiring integer arithmetic). Failure modes emerge when occlusion causes vector norms to vanish, creating singularities in the arccosine function, or when aggressive quantization destroys the subtle gradients necessary for distinguishing fine motor errors.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The system models two distinct agents: the athlete (the physical actor attempting to minimize biomechanical error) and the AI coach (the observer optimizing for informational fidelity). The AI must anticipate the athlete's intent by projecting their current noisy state onto a manifold of professional movements. The feedback loop assumes the athlete acts as a rational agent who will adjust their trajectory upon receiving statistically significant visual biofeedback.
